$comment: Source register. `method` explains how we know: fetched = this agent retrieved the page from the publisher's own domain on fetched_on; api = observed by calling a published API; operator = supplied in the brief; local = measured inside the build sandbox; referenced = URL appears inside a fetched page but was not opened by us. Fields that no row here supports stay blank on the site and get a FLG entry.

sources.title: Associates Program Operating Agreement
sources.why_it_matters: It is the agreement this site would be operating under. Section 5 fixes the disclosure wording; Section 1 defines the only permitted link format.

quotes.text: The links must properly use the special “tagged” link formats we provide and comply with this Agreement (“Special Links”).

You must clearly and prominently state the following, or any substantially similar statement previously allowed under this Agreement, on your Site or any other location where Amazon may authorize your display or other use of Program Content: “As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases.”
You will not misrepresent or embellish our relationship with you (including by expressing or implying that we support, sponsor, or endorse you)…

For the avoidance of doubt and without limitation for purposes of the foregoing subsection (a) any violation of Section 5 and as specified in the Program Policies will be deemed a material breach of this Agreement.
…(b) review, monitor, crawl, and otherwise investigate your Site to verify compliance with this Agreement…

sources.title: Associates Program Policies (Commission Income Statement; Participation Requirements; Products Statement)
sources.why_it_matters: This single page decides most of the architecture: what a link may look like, whether a price or a star rating may be shown, what disqualifies a sale, and what counts as unsuitable content.

quotes.text: …beginning when a customer clicks through that Special Link and ending upon the first to occur of the following: (x) 24 hours elapse from that click, (y) the customer places an order for a Product… or (z) the customer clicks through a Special Link to an Amazon Site that is not your Special Link…
…completing the order for that Product no later than 89 days after their initial click-through of the Special Link…
within 180 days of the purchase, the Product is shipped to, streamed or downloaded by, and paid for by the customer

quotes.ref: Commission Income Statement §2(c) — Prohibited Paid Search Placement
quotes.text: …any Product order where… a customer who is referred to an Amazon Site through any advertisement that you purchased, including through participation in bidding or auctions on keywords, search terms, or other identifiers that include the word “amazon”, or “kindle”, or any other Amazon Mark…

any Product purchased by a customer who is referred to an Amazon Site by a link that is generated or displayed on a search engine (including Google, Yahoo, Bing, or any other search portal, sponsored advertising service, or other search or referral service, or any site that participates in such search engine’s network)…
…a link that sends users indirectly to an Amazon Site via an intermediate site, without requiring the customer to click on a link or take some other affirmative action on that intermediate site…
any Product purchase that is not correctly tracked or reported because the links from your site to the relevant Amazon Site are not properly formatted
any pre-release or pre-order Product that is not available on a Product listing page.

Your Site(s) must contain original content and be publicly available via the website address provided in the application. Original content utilizing third-party materials must contain significant commentary, analysis, or transformation to any materials you include.

(g) include any trademark of Amazon or its affiliates, or a variant or misspelling of a trademark of Amazon or its affiliates in any domain name, subdomain name, in any “tag” or Associates ID, or in any username, group name, or other identifier on any social networking site…

You must not encourage customers to bookmark your Special Links. All Special Links must be accessed directly from your Site. For example, you must include your Associates ID or “tag” (appearing as XXXXX-##, or such other format as we may designate) as a parameter in the URL of each link you place on your Site to an Amazon Site.

quotes.ref: Participation Requirements §2(b) — sub-tags and end users
quotes.text: Under no circumstances may you associate any sub-tag, other ID or reporting provided in connection with the Associates Program with a specific end user of your Site (e.g. you may not dynamically assign sub-tags to users as they arrive on your Site for purposes of monitoring such users’ behavior).

quotes.ref: Participation Requirements §2(b) — what a Special Link may point at
quotes.text: Special Links must link to Products (as defined in the Products Statement). When linking to pages with Product lists you must have additional original content on your Site that is relevant to the Special Link.
You must not make inaccurate, overbroad, deceptive or otherwise misleading claims about any Product, an Amazon Site, or any of our policies, promotions, or prices.

…your Site may only show prices and availability if: (a) we serve the link in which that price and availability data are displayed, or (b) you obtain Product pricing and availability data via Creators API or PA API and you comply with the requirements regarding use of Creators API or PA API in the License.

…if you choose to display prices for any Product on your Site in any “comparison” format… you must display both the lowest “new” price and, if we provide it to you, the lowest “used” price at which the Product is available on the Amazon Site.
You must remove from your Site any links and related references to limited time promotions as soon as that promotion on the relevant Amazon Site ends.

disclosing on your Site accurately and adequately and otherwise satisfying applicable legal requirements, either through a privacy policy or otherwise, the use of cookies, pixels, and other technologies by you and third parties…

quotes.ref: Participation Requirements §4 — offline and solicited messages
quotes.text: You will not engage in any Promotional Activities in any offline manner… You may include Special Links in emails, SMS and direct messaging from your social media Sites; provided, that such communications are solicited (i.e., opted into by the receiving customer)…

quotes.ref: Participation Requirements §5 — software, devices and machine learning
quotes.text: You will not, without or express prior written approval, use, or allow any third party to use, any Special Links or Program Content to develop machine learning models or related technology.

quotes.ref: Participation Requirements §6(a) — Program Content must not be altered
quotes.text: You will not add to, delete from, or otherwise alter any Program Content in any way, including by adding additional information, except that you may resize Program Content consisting of a graphic image in a manner that maintains the original proportions of the image or truncate Program Content consisting of text in a manner that does not materially alter the meaning of the text…
You will promptly remove from your Site and delete or otherwise destroy any Program Content that is no longer displayed on an Amazon Site or that we notify you is no longer available for your use.

You will not offer any person or entity any consideration, reward, or incentive (including any money, rebate, discount, points, donation to charity or other organization, or other benefit) for using Special Links.

You will not frame an Amazon Site, or any part of it, within your Site… You will not post or serve any Special Links or other content promoting an Amazon Site within any pop-up or pop-under windows, transitional page ads, or layer ads…
You will not artificially generate clicks or impressions on your Site or create Sessions on an Amazon Site, whether by way of a robot or software program or otherwise.

quotes.ref: Participation Requirements §6(t) — reviews and star ratings
quotes.text: You will not display or otherwise use any of our customer reviews or star ratings, in part or in whole, on your Site unless you have obtained a link to that customer review or star rating through Creators API or PA API and you comply with the requirements for Creators API and PA API described in the License.

You will not directly or indirectly purchase any Product(s) or take a Bounty Event action through Special Links, whether for your use or for the use of any other person or entity, and you will not permit, request or encourage any of your friends, relatives, employees, contractors, or business relations to directly or indirectly purchase any Product(s)…

You will not cloak, hide, spoof, or otherwise obscure the URL of your Site containing Special Links (including by use of Redirecting Links)… You will not use a link shortening service, button, hyperlink or other ad placement in a manner that makes it unclear that you are linking to an Amazon Site.
Unless otherwise agreed by Amazon, your Site must not have price tracking and/or price alerting functionality.
Under the Associates Program, subject to the additions and exclusions described in this Products Statement, a “Product” is any physical or digital item sold on an Amazon Site.

quotes.ref: Commission Income Statement §6 — Payment Minimum Chart
quotes.text: U.S. — Minimum: Option 1 (Deposit) 10 USD; Option 2 (Gift Card) 10 USD, maximum 2000 USD; Option 3 (Check) 100 USD; Check Processing Fee 15 USD.

If at any time there has been no substantial activity on your account for at least 3 years, then we will have the right, with 7 days’ written notice to withhold the accrued commission income for your inactive account…

Unsuitable Sites include those that: (a) promote or contain sexually explicit or obscene materials, (b) promote violence…, (c) promote or contain false, deceptive, libelous or defamatory materials… (f) are directed toward children or knowingly collect, use, or disclose personal information from children under 13 years of age…

sources.title: Help: Why do I have to identify myself as an Associate? How should I do this on social media?
sources.why_it_matters: Amazon's own answer tells an associate what a link-level disclosure looks like in practice, which is the thing a page template has to get right.

quotes.text: 1. Clear. A clear disclosure could be as simple as "(paid link)", "#ad", or "#CommissionsEarned". 2. Conspicuous. It should be placed near any affiliate link or product review in a location that customers will notice easily. They shouldn't have to hunt for it.
It is important to remember that the disclosure must be made in the medium in which the recommendation was provided…

sources.title: FTC's Endorsement Guides: What People Are Asking
sources.why_it_matters: The disclosure duty here is not only contractual. This is the regulator's own statement of why a material connection must be visible next to the recommendation.

quotes.text: …if there's a connection between an endorser and the marketer that a significant minority of consumers wouldn't expect and it would affect how they evaluate the endorsement, that connection should be disclosed clearly and conspicuously.
…the Guides say, an endorsement must reflect the honest opinion of the endorser and can't be used to make a claim the marketer of the product couldn't legally make.

sources.title: Welcome to Creators API — operations and prerequisites
sources.why_it_matters: It states the prerequisite for any automated price/review/commission pipeline, and it is the reason this build sequences content before automation rather than the reverse.

quotes.text: 1. Be enrolled in the Amazon Associates program for your target marketplace 2. Have at least 10 qualifying sales within the past 30 days to access the PA API through the Creators API
GetItems — Retrieve detailed information for specific products by ASIN or other identifiers

sources.title: PA-API 5 Deprecation Notice
sources.why_it_matters: Kills the obvious implementation path (a PA-API 5 client) so nobody spends a session building on a retired endpoint.

quotes.text: The Amazon Product Advertising API 5.0 (PA-API 5) has been deprecated and is being replaced by the Creators API. New and existing integrations should move to the Creators API to continue accessing Amazon's product catalog.

quotes.ref: What you'll see if you still call PA-API 5
quotes.text: Applications that continue to call PA-API 5 receive an HTTP 403 Forbidden response with an AccessDeniedException

sources.title: Article (Article, NewsArticle, BlogPosting) structured data
sources.why_it_matters: Defines the markup our generator emits and which properties are actually read (author, dates, image), so the feed and schema are built to a published spec instead of guesswork.

quotes.text: Adding Article structured data to your news, blog, and sports article pages can help Google understand more about the web page and show better title text, images, and date information for the article in search results…

sources.title: Creating helpful, reliable, people-first content
sources.why_it_matters: The published bar we hold our own copy to — and the documented reason "generated-sounding" filler is a ranking risk, not just a taste problem.

quotes.text: Does the content provide original information, reporting, research, or analysis? … Does the main heading or page title avoid exaggerating or being shocking in nature?

sources.title: What is GitHub Pages?
sources.why_it_matters: Two consequences for this build: a project site is served from a sub-path (so every link must be relative), and the host logs visitor IP addresses (so the privacy page cannot claim 'no data leaves the browser').

quotes.ref: Types of GitHub Pages sites, table
quotes.text: Default site location … `http(s)://<owner>.github.io/<repositoryname>`
When a GitHub Pages site is visited, the visitor's IP address is logged and stored for security purposes, regardless of whether the visitor has signed into GitHub or not.

sources.title: Qualify your outbound links
sources.why_it_matters: Defines rel="sponsored", which the brief requires on every product link, and states the real effect: marked links are generally not followed. It is also the reason we can say plainly that the marking costs us no affiliate traffic — attribution rides on the tag parameter, not on Google.

quotes.text: Mark links that are advertisements or paid placements (commonly called paid links) with the sponsored value.

Links marked with these rel attributes will generally not be followed. Remember that the linked pages may be found through other means, such as sitemaps or links from other sites, and thus they may still be crawled.

sources.title: ASIN / product identifier definition (10-character convention)
sources.why_it_matters: The brief leans on 'Amazon's ASIN definition provides a checkable identifier'. The length rule it implies is real and widely documented, but this session could not open a page stating it, so FLG-001 reports the observed shape and stops there instead of asserting invalidity.
